subject: Post-demo: model fit proposals + multilingual QA plan (Luminova / Kajiya)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc:
Date: 2026-10-28T14:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo recap + ask: model recommendations & multilingual QA plan (Luminova / Kajiya)

Team — quick recap from this morning's discovery with Luminova (Sylvie) and Kajiya (Hiro): solid product fit (multilingual knowledge assistant for marketing operations). Key notes: EU data residency required, primary languages: French/Spanish/German; secondary APAC test: Japanese/Korean for a subset of customers.

Customer ask:
- Baseline models that meet hallucination and latency targets for support-style prompts (concise answers, citations).
- A small PoC benchmark across the target locales using their prompt set (attached: luminova_prompt_set_v1.json).
- Sizing guidance for a 30k monthly active users pilot (in-region).

My suggested starting configuration (based on their latency SLO ~ <400ms p95 for short answers and 99% availability):
- Candidate models: redwood-lrc-3b (fp16), redwood-v2-small-q4 (quantized low-latency variant), and for higher-quality fallback redwood-v2-medium.
- Quantization: run q4_0 and q8_0 trials — we expect 20–40% token-cost improvement with small latency changes; include a baseline fp16 run.
- Routing: EU requests pinned to EU Dedicated pool; fall back to hosted regionally only if Dedicated saturation > 80%.

Proposed evals (short):
1) Multilingual correctness and hallucination rate (chrF/ROUGE-style + human spot checks).
2) Latency p50/p95, cold-start for KV cache where applicable.
3) Cost per 1k QPS token mix simulations using the customer's prompt length distribution (see sheet multiregion_benchmark_matrix.xlsx).

Attachments: luminova_prompt_set_v1.json; multiregion_benchmark_matrix.xlsx; security_q_20261028.pdf (they already sent initial security questions).

Next steps I proposed to the buyer: run a 1-week focused benchmark per model (3 candidates) on their prompt set with French/Spanish as priority, report metrics and a recommended playbook for Dedicated vs Hosted. They asked for a short pricing sketch and a timeline for an EU-only PoC.

Action items for us:
- Rishi: pricing/contract sketch + tentative Dedicated capacity sizing.
- Priyom: technical plan for running the multiregion benchmarks and expected instrumentation (traces, token-level cost breakdown).
- Grace: coordinate security/compliance answers and confirm EU data handling options.

I'll draft an outbound to Sylvie confirming the plan once we align internally.

— Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: model recommendations & multilingual QA plan (Luminova / Kajiya)

Quick technical plan — high level. I'll run the benchmarks and hand off a results matrix. Plan:

Scope per locale (FR/ES/DE and JP/KR subset):
- Unit tests: 200 synthetic QA prompts per language (from luminova_prompt_set_v1.json) covering support queries, marketing summarization, and citation requests.
- Human eval slices: 60 human checks per language focusing on hallucination and factuality.
- Metrics: accuracy/intent-match, hallucination rate (binary label), fluency (1–5), latency p50/p95, token-cost estimate. We'll output chrF and a simple answer-exact-match where applicable.

Model runs (parallel):
- redwood-lrc-3b (fp16) — baseline quality.
- redwood-v2-small-q4 — low-latency quantized baseline.
- redwood-v2-medium (fp16) — higher-quality candidate when fallback desired.

GPU hours estimate (rough): per model per locale for 1-week active runs: 18–28 GPU-hours (small/quantized lower). I'll provide a precise table after the first dry-run.

Instrumentation we need from the customer: sample production prompts (we have), expected concurrency, and an anonymized dataset of ~1k real queries per locale if possible — that will make the benchmark realistic. Also need an account-level token mix for cost sims.

Note on latency & KV cache: if their conversational flows rely on long context for citations, p95 will spike unless we enable prefix KV caching and use a medium model for long-history cases. We'll include a KV cache experiment.

Drive: I'll drop the initial notebook and a README to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDef-benchmark-notebooks (internal).

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Bonjour Camila,

Thanks for the summary and to your team for the quick follow-up. We agree with the proposed three-model approach. A few clarifications:

1) Data residency: for pilot we require logs and model outputs to be stored in-region (EU). Is the Dedicated EU pool fully separated for logs and backups? We prefer not to have backups leave region.

2) Timeline: procurement is aiming for a decision within 4 weeks. We can do the 1-week benchmark early November if you can provide a PoC SOW and the pricing sketch by Friday (2026-11-05).

3) On-prem question: Kajiya mentioned some customers may ask for an on-prem connector. For the pilot we only need EU Dedicated but want the option to discuss on-prem in January.

4) Sample data: we can share an anonymized set of 1,200 French queries this Friday. Do you accept an encrypted S3 share or prefer Drive?

We'll also need a short NDA (we have a standard one) and an SOW to hand to procurement.

— Sylvie Laroche
Head of Platform, Luminova
